citation: J. Seymour Currey, The Story of Old Fort Dearborn. Chicago: A. C. McClurg & Co., 1912 (published August 1912). A popular history of the first fort from 1803 to its burning in 1812, compiled from the printed accounts and the pioneer recollections before it, with eleven illustrations.
author: J. Seymour Currey (1844-1929)
describes_date: Chicago and the first Fort Dearborn, 1803-1812

what_it_does_not_supply: an eyewitness: Currey writes a century after the farm, from the books before him, and he says so ('it is said in a recent history of Chicago')
a survey distance. 'Some four miles' is a round figure, and the book gives no route for it
the illustration's own date or maker, which the caption does not state; until it is read it is a retrospective picture and grades tier 5 as a picture, whatever this record's tier as a text
note: Graded tier 3 as a compiled secondary history drawn from pioneer testimony, the rung the ladder gives Andreas. It places the farm independently of Hubbard's 'half a mile below Bridgeport' only in its wording: it may rest on the same tradition, and nothing here claims the two agree because they are independent.
